sketches.title: Graveyard Shift CV
sketches.premise: Each round, the Host announces a real but grimly ordinary job opening. You and your rival submit one line from a CV applying for it, then the Host crowns the applicant whose line wanders furthest from sensible self-preservation without losing the job’s required duty. Ceremonial applause for the desperate; medical concern for everyone else.
sketches.criterion: The CV line must still show that the applicant will perform the card’s named duty in the card’s named setting.
sketches.move_shape: Write one CV claim, boast, or experience line under 90 characters; for “Clean the school toilets at midnight,” write: “I bring my own mop, a torch, and absolutely no questions.”
sketches.first_card: Remove chewing gum from cinema seats after the final showing.

sketches.title: Reference Check from Hell
sketches.premise: A job nobody wants comes with a dull fact about its work. Both players write a reference from a former boss, and the Host decides who turns that fact into the strangest recommendation while still accidentally recommending the applicant for the job. The seal is stamped; the applicant is doomed.
sketches.criterion: The reference must still make the applicant suitable and willing to do the card’s stated job.
sketches.move_shape: Write one reference sentence under 90 characters; for “Count escaped chickens at a farm gate,” write: “Punctual, fearless, and already knows every chicken by its alias.”
sketches.first_card: Stand outside a nightclub and hold umbrellas for strangers in the rain.

sketches.title: Orientation Day
sketches.premise: The Host gives you the first dull instruction for a terrible new job. You answer with one line the new worker says on their first day, and the Host rewards the line that builds the wildest world around the work while obeying the instruction. Welcome aboard, you poor bastard.
sketches.criterion: The line must still have the worker carrying out the card’s exact instruction.
sketches.move_shape: Write one spoken line under 90 characters; for “Photograph potholes for the council,” write: “Smile, crater—today you become evidence in my revenge.”
sketches.first_card: Sort lost socks at a hotel laundry.

sketches.title: Union of One
sketches.premise: A job advert offers one bleak duty. You and your rival each write a tiny union demand for taking it, and the Host scores the demand that travels furthest while leaving the duty recognisable and accepted. The ceremony begins with a handshake and ends with a grievance.
sketches.criterion: The demand must still accept that the worker will do the card’s named duty.
sketches.move_shape: Write one demand under 90 characters; for “Dress as a scarecrow outside a garden centre,” write: “Hazard pay, a heated hat, and the right to frighten managers too.”
sketches.first_card: Collect dog mess from a public park before sunrise.

sketches.title: The Worst Perk
sketches.premise: The Host announces a miserable job and asks for one perk the employer might advertise to lure applicants. Both players pitch a perk, and the Host rewards the pitch that becomes most gloriously unreasonable without changing what the worker must do. No one gets dental.
sketches.criterion: The perk must leave the card’s job and its required duty intact rather than replacing or denying them.
sketches.move_shape: Write one advertised perk under 90 characters; for “Answer complaints at a haunted hotel,” write: “Free ghost insurance, plus one paid scream per shift.”
sketches.first_card: Test supermarket trolleys for wheel wobble.

sketches.title: Resignation Letter
sketches.premise: You have survived one day in a job nobody wants. The Host supplies the one dull thing you were hired to do; you and your rival write a resignation line that still admits you did it, then compete to make the excuse most magnificently unhinged. The Host reads the minutes in a solemn voice.
sketches.criterion: The resignation must still confirm that the writer performed the card’s stated job duty.
sketches.move_shape: Write one resignation sentence under 90 characters; for “Wake the town clock each morning,” write: “I resign: the clock is awake, and so is every damn neighbour.”
sketches.first_card: Watch a supermarket car park for abandoned trolleys.
